name: Agenda
description: Your calendar and your tasks as a projection of the personal vault: upcoming events from the vault's events, proposals, answers and cancellation asks, and the task board from the vault's own tasks, all through consent-checked typed commands. No data of its own — revoke the grant and the app goes dark.

vault.why: Shows your upcoming schedule and your task list, and lets you propose, move, and respond to events and add, finish and organise tasks.

actions.name: propose
phrasings: put lunch with Sam on Friday at noon
add a dentist appointment next Tuesday at 3pm
schedule a team sync every Monday morning
actions.description: Propose an event through event.propose: its title, when (an instant, or a wall clock in a zone), an optional repeat rule, guests, place, link and reminders. Refused when a busy event would land on another busy one; a free event blocks nothing.

id.description: The id the shell minted for this write (#922 G2); omitted, the vault mints one.

rule.description: An RFC 5545 recurrence rule; the vault refuses one it cannot expand.

attendees.description: The people invited, by person id.

starts.description: An instant (...Z), a wall clock in `zone`, a floating wall clock, or a date for an all-day event.

ends.description: Exclusive for a timed event; the LAST day, inclusive, for an all-day one.

zone.description: An IANA zone; with it a wall clock is that zone's.

actions.name: rsvp
phrasings: mark me tentative for the offsite
actions.description: Record one guest's answer to an event through event.respond: accepted, declined or tentative.

actions.name: edit-event
phrasings: rename the dentist event to checkup
add a note to Friday's dinner that it's at Luigi's
actions.description: Revise an event through event.edit. A key that is present is set (null clears it); a key that is absent is left alone. A change to the series that would leave a skipped or moved day matching nothing is refused.

rule.description: An RFC 5545 recurrence rule; the vault refuses one it cannot expand.

attendees.description: The people invited, by person id.

starts.description: An instant (...Z), a wall clock in `zone`, a floating wall clock, or a date for an all-day event.

ends.description: Exclusive for a timed event; the LAST day, inclusive, for an all-day one.

zone.description: An IANA zone; with it a wall clock is that zone's.

actions.name: edit-occurrence
actions.description: Skip, move, rename or put back one day of a repeating event through event.edit_occurrence, keyed by the series-local wall clock the rule produced (`original_start`). Scope `occurrence` is that day, `future` is that day and every one after it, `series` is the whole event.

original_start.description: The series-local wall clock the rule produced for the day.

starts.description: An instant (...Z), a wall clock in `zone`, a floating wall clock, or a date for an all-day event.

ends.description: Exclusive for a timed event; the LAST day, inclusive, for an all-day one.

zone.description: An IANA zone; with it a wall clock is that zone's.

actions.name: cancel-event
actions.description: Cancel an event through event.cancel: a status its guests see, not a deletion (the trash is entity.trash).

actions.name: trash-event
phrasings: remove the team offsite from my calendar
actions.description: Move an event to the trash through entity.trash; restore-event brings it back.

actions.name: restore-event
actions.description: Bring a trashed event back through entity.restore.

actions.name: attach
phrasings: attach the menu to Friday's dinner
add the boarding pass to my flight event
attach the agenda doc to the team sync
actions.description: Attach or detach any Agenda item (an event or a task) through the shared edge verbs.

actions.name: detach
phrasings: detach the menu from Friday's dinner
remove the boarding pass from my flight event
take the agenda doc off the team sync
actions.description: Attach or detach any Agenda item (an event or a task) through the shared edge verbs.

actions.name: add-task
phrasings: remind me to call the plumber tomorrow
add a task to buy milk
put 'file taxes' on my list for April 15
actions.description: Add a task through task.add: dated, prioritized, estimated, repeating, reminded, filed in a project and section, or as a subtask of an open top-level task.

id.description: The id the shell minted for this write (#922 G2); omitted, the vault mints one.

due.description: A day, a wall clock or an instant.

rule.description: An RFC 5545 recurrence rule; the vault refuses one it cannot expand, and a repeating task needs a due date.

actions.name: edit-task
phrasings: add a note to the taxes task
actions.description: Edit a task's title, note, due date, priority, effort, reminder lead time or repeat rule through task.edit. A key that is present is set (null clears it); a key that is absent is left alone.

due.description: A day, a wall clock or an instant.

rule.description: An RFC 5545 recurrence rule; the vault refuses one it cannot expand, and a repeating task needs a due date.

actions.name: complete-task
actions.description: Complete a task through task.complete: the one completion operation Tasks, People and automations share. A repeating task gets its next occurrence, carrying its project, tags and what it is about; completing a completed task changes nothing.

actions.name: reopen-task
phrasings: the taxes aren't done after all
actions.description: Reopen a completed or cancelled task through task.reopen; it spawns nothing.

actions.name: cancel-task
phrasings: I'm not buying milk anymore, drop it
cancel this week's repeat of the laundry task
actions.description: Cancel a task through task.cancel: it ends this occurrence with no successor (the Logbook's Won't do).

actions.name: organize-task
phrasings: put the plumber task in the Home project
move the taxes task to the Finance project
actions.description: File a task through task.organize: its project and section (null is the Inbox), its place in the list, and what a repeat counts from. Moving to another project leaves the section behind unless one is named.

actions.name: delete-task
actions.description: Move a task and its subtasks to the 30-day trash through entity.trash; the Logbook keeps nothing.

actions.name: purge-task
phrasings: permanently delete the trashed milk task
actions.description: Delete a trashed task and the subtasks trashed with it forever through entity.purge (#1015 D1); a subtask restored on its own is promoted to a top-level task first.

actions.name: restore-task
actions.description: Bring a trashed task back through entity.restore, with the subtasks trashed with it; a subtask trashed on its own stays where it was.

actions.name: create-project
phrasings: make a project called Home renovation
start a Finance project in the Personal area
actions.description: Create a project or an area through container.create. A project may sit in an area (its `parent`), and has a color and a place in the list.

actions.name: rename-list
phrasings: rename the Home renovation project to House projects
actions.description: Retitle a project or an area through entity.retitle.

actions.name: create-section
phrasings: add a section called Kitchen to Home renovation
create a Waiting section in Errands
add a Q4 section to Finance
actions.description: Create a section within a task project through container.create (the project is its `parent`).

actions.name: add-task-tag
phrasings: tag the plumber task as home
add the tag urgent to the taxes task
actions.description: Tag a task through tag.add: a free-form label shared with every other app that tags; minted on first use. Idempotent.

actions.name: remove-task-tag
phrasings: remove the home tag from the plumber task
take the urgent label off the taxes task
actions.description: Remove one tag from a task through tag.remove; the tag survives for other things.

actions.name: follow-calendar
phrasings: sync events from the calendar on this phone
pull in this week's events from my calendars
actions.description: Follow the phone's calendars through follow.calendar, one calendar at a time: a field the member never changed follows the phone, one they changed stands, an event the vault does not know is matched by title and start before one is added, a repeating series is one event with its rule and the days the phone skipped or moved, and one gone from a complete read goes to the trash if the member never edited it.

queries.name: upcoming
queries.description: Non-cancelled events, soonest first, with the calendars they could land on, each event's calendar_id, link, reminders, its attachments and its guest list (each `{party_id, name, partstat, is_you}`, read from the event's attendee edges). Defaults to today forward; pass ISO `from`/`to` instants to read any visible range (month and week views do), including still-running multi-day events that began before `from`. A repeating event (rule set) is materialized into one row per occurrence inside the visible range, each carrying the series' real event_id, an `instance_key` for list render and the `original_start_local` an occurrence edit is keyed on; a skipped day is left out and a moved one is where it moved to. Every occurrence also carries where it falls in the request's `tz`.

queries.name: search
queries.description: Full-text search over events and tasks through the vault's one index — the ranked non-cancelled events (title, description and place) in the upcoming row shape, and the ranked tasks (title, description and project) in the board's row shape, each with a hit snippet, never a whole-table pull.

queries.name: day-context
queries.description: The cross-app facts that decorate a calendar day, as one read-only projection: birthdays recurring inside the window (each `{party_id, name, month, day, tier}`, where `tier` is `inner` when the owner starred that person and `outer` otherwise), and holidays. Holidays are always `[]` today — the vault has no holiday source. It reads no task: a dated task is a row in its day, read from `tasks.board`. `from`/`to` are inclusive `YYYY-MM-DD` days, defaulting to today plus 45 days and capped at a 400-day span.

queries.name: parties
queries.description: Pickable people for the invite picker — each `{party_id, name, is_you}`, you sorted first. `me` is the owner's person id. No event data; just the directory the create-event attendee multi-select draws from.

queries.name: event
queries.description: One event, or one occurrence of a repeating one: the row the detail screen draws, with its calendar.

queries.name: board
queries.description: The task board as a bounded window (newest open tasks by creation, caller-sized, families kept whole; the logbook read is capped at its visible 50 most recently closed), each row carrying its tags (`[{concept_id, label}]`) and what it is about, plus the distinct tag list (`[{concept_id, label}]`) seen within the window — never a whole-table pull; `truncated` is the open walk's own cursor — it exists or it does not — rather than a guess from the row count.

view.description: How the rows are grouped; the rows are the same board read whichever is asked.

queries.name: task
queries.description: One task by id, whether or not any board window holds it: the task with its subtasks, tags, project and section, and its parent when it is a subtask.

queries.name: projects
queries.description: The live projects and their sections, with open counts, in their order.

queries.name: catch-up
queries.description: What fell behind while the member was away: dated work past due, repeating work that missed occurrences, and undated work sitting too long, each as a pile.

queries.name: trash
queries.description: The tasks in the 30-day trash, most recently trashed first, each with when it was deleted and when it is erased.
